sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Law of Tolerance (Shelford's Law)**: Organisms have an optimal range of environmental conditions; survival decreases as conditions deviate from the **optimum**.
• **Liebig’s Law of the Minimum**: Growth is dictated not by total resources, but by the **limiting factor** (the scarcest resource).
• **Competitive Exclusion Principle (Gause's Law)**: Two species competing for the exact same **niche** cannot coexist indefinitely; one will eventually be displaced.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: **Trophic Efficiency** (usually ~10% energy transfer between levels) dictates the length of food chains.

items.definition: The functional role and position of a species within its habitat, including its resource use and interactions. It is the 'profession' of the organism.
A transition zone between two biomes or ecosystems. It exhibits the 'Edge Effect', where species diversity is often higher than in adjacent communities.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA)**: Using biodiversity and ecosystem services to help people adapt to climate change.
• **Restoration Ecology**: Active intervention to recover degraded ecosystems (e.g., Compensatory Afforestation Fund - CAMPA).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Habitat fragmentation, invasive species, and anthropogenic nitrogen loading.
• **Solutions**: Connectivity conservation (wildlife corridors) and Nature-based Solutions (NbS).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'TEN' (Trophic Efficiency Norm).
• **Decoded Meaning**: 10% energy transfer, Energy flows one-way, Nutrients cycle.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Habitat' (address) with 'Niche' (profession). Remember: Two species can share a habitat, but not the exact same niche.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Anthropocene' to describe the current geological epoch where human activity is the dominant influence on ecological principles.

keyTakeaways: Energy flows linearly through ecosystems while nutrients cycle continuously.
Biodiversity is the insurance policy of an ecosystem, enhancing resilience against disturbances.
The 'Edge Effect' in ecotones is a critical concept for protected area management.
